Ezra Zedi, son of Saada and Moshe, was born in 1950 in Aden, Yemen. He is the brother of Yoel, Avraham and Amnon. Four older sisters died in childhood.

When he was a month old, the family immigrated to Israel. They were absorbed into the Ein Shemer transit camp, and later moved to Ra'anana, where Ezra grew up and was educated. At high school he studied literature.

In 1968 he was drafted into the IDF and assigned to the Infantry Corps. He served most of his military service in the Golan Heights.

Later, during his reserve service, he took part in the Yom Kippur War in October 1973.

After his discharge from the IDF, he joined the Prison Service and served at the Ashmoret prison. After several years in this role he transferred to serve in the Israel Police, first as an escort for detainees and later as a youth guard at the Abu Kabir detention facility.

In 1976 he married Shoshana, and the couple had four children: Miriam, Moshe, Michal and Mirav. Ezra was a loving husband and a devoted father. On Shabbat, all the family members would spend time together, on trips around Israel and visits with relatives.

Ezra was gifted with his hands and loved handiwork, carpentry in particular. He also loved football and would watch matches at the football stadium in Ra'anana.

Sergeant First Class Ezra HaLevi Zedi fell during his service on 25 Heshvan 5747 (26 November 1986). He was thirty-six years old. He was laid to rest in the military cemetery in Ra'anana. He left behind a wife, three daughters, a son and three brothers.

Ezra is commemorated in the Police building in Jaffa, in the Tel Aviv District memorial corner for fallen officers of the Israel Police, and at the memorial to the fallen of the Israel Police in Beit Shemesh. He is also commemorated on the Israel Police Fallen memorial website.
